t: This is Hyde Park Gate, two parallel roads running south from Kensington Road, along the edge of Kensington Gardens. The street has a literary pedigree. Julia Stephen, mother of Virginia Woolf and Vanessa Bell, lived and died here. The novelist and playwright Margaret Kennedy, who wrote The Constant Nymph, was born here, and so was the portraitist Sir Arthur Stockdale Cope. Sir Roderick Jones, who spent most of his career at Reuters, lived and died here as well.
